text: Harbour City starts strong, scoring twice just before and after halftime. Elias Okafor, positioned around 14 metres from Seabrook Town’s goal on the left side, nets the first from a precise through ball from Marek Barros. Shortly after, Barros extends the lead with a long-range cross-shot from near the right flank. Seabrook Town responds quickly, Tariq Marlowe scoring inside the penalty area just 9 metres from goal after a turnover. Following a tactical switch at 65 minutes by Seabrook to press higher and play more direct, Callum Varga taps in an equaliser from the right flank. Into stoppage time, Kian Romano fires two decisive goals in quick succession from close range near the central goal area, completing a dramatic comeback. Marek Barros earns player of the match for his all-around performance in midfield and attack. Harbour City’s red card at 43 minutes weakened their defense, aiding Seabrook’s late resurgence. The final score is Seabrook Town 4, Harbour City 2[#905][#975][#1104][#1448][#1882][#1906][#871].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for audio audience in en

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals against Harbour City's 2, winning the match 4-2 [#1906].
- Marek Barros of Harbour City delivered an outstanding performance with 1 goal, 2 assists, 9 interceptions, and a 9.8 rating [#1906].
- Seabrook Town had significantly higher expected goals (xG) at 3.48 compared to Harbour City's 1.0 [#1906].
- A red card was issued to Joon Whitfield of Harbour City in the 43rd minute, potentially impacting their defense [#871].
- Kian Romano scored two late goals for Seabrook Town in stoppage time, securing the win [#1906].

- Harbour City’s first goal at 45’ came from a long, patient build-up involving 17 passes over nearly a minute, reflecting their 4-2-3-1 formation and "patient short passing" style. The goal was finished by Elias Okafor from a through ball by Marek Barros, highlighting their emphasis on possession retention and careful chance creation [#904,#905].

- Marek Barros’ second goal for Harbour City, scored just after halftime, originated from a corner (a set piece) with a quick cross, showing their ability to capitalize on dead-ball situations despite their patient style. This indicates tactical flexibility to use set pieces as scoring opportunities [#973,#975].

- Seabrook Town’s goals often came from faster transitions and regains: their first goal at 53’ was immediate off a ball recovery by Tariq Marlowe, reflecting a more direct approach even before their tactical change. This aligns with their 3-4-3 formation and "wide, crossing play" style emphasizing quick attacks down the wings [#1103,#1104].

- After falling behind, Seabrook’s coach implemented a tactical adjustment at 65’ to press higher and play more direct with a higher defensive line. This shift led to increased ball recoveries in advanced positions and more effective chances, evidenced by equalizing and late winning goals scored in quick counter or direct attacks, notably Kian Romano’s 90+2’ goal from a counter-attack after a regain [#1361,#1881,#1882].

- The increased pressing and directness post-tactical change fits Seabrook Town’s aggressive 3-4-3 layout, using their wide players to deliver crosses or incisive through balls, culminating in two late goals by Kian Romano involving short assists and quick passing sequences [#1905,#1906].
